task.title: Configure Artifactory to use the Lightwell Network Python repository
task.shortdesc: Configure JFrog Artifactory to proxy the Lightwell Network Python repository so that your organization's build tools resolve dependencies through your centralized Artifactory instance.

ul.li: You have administrator access to your JFrog Artifactory instance.
You have an active Lightwell Network membership.
You have created a Lightwell Network service account. For more information, see
You have chosen the repository tier that matches your environment. For more information, see

Your Artifactory naming policy allows the .rhlw-0000X version suffix, for example, 5.2.17.rhlw-00003 or 5.2.17.rhlw-00001-n0003 depending on your repository. These suffixes are the standard identifiers for Lightwell-patched libraries.

step.cmd: In the JFrog Platform console, navigate to Administration Repository.
Click Create a Repository and select Local.
Select PyPI as the package type.
On the Basic tab, set the following values:

substep.cmd: In the Repository Key field, enter lightwell-python-validated.
In the URL field, enter the following URL:https://packages.redhat.com/api/pulp-content/lightwell/python/validated/
In the Registry URL field, enter the following URL:https://packages.redhat.com/lightwell/python/validated/
Leave the Registry Index Location URL Suffix at the default value of simple
In the User Name field, enter your registry service account username in the format XXXXXXX|service-account-name.
In the Password / Access Token field, enter your registry service account token.

step.cmd: Leave the remaining fields at their default values.

ul.li: Navigate to the lightwell-remote repository in your Artifactory instance and verify that artifacts are being cached from the Lightwell Network repository.
Configure your Python build tool to resolve packages through your Artifactory instance. For instructions on connecting your PyPI client to Artifactory, see Connect Your PyPI Client to Artifactory
